official.deadline_note: As of 2027 there are two calls per year: the first, launched mid-February, closes on the last Wednesday of April at 14:00 CET (listed as 28-04-2027 14:00 CET), decisions are communicated in July and funded projects must start no later than 1 February of the following year; the second, launched mid-September, closes on the last Wednesday of November at 14:00 CET, decisions are communicated in March of the following year and funded projects must start no later than 1 October.
official.application_cycle: Very first call launched mid-September 2026, deadline 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET; next listed deadline 28 April 2027 at 14:00 CET
official.status_note: The very first AFdoc call was launched in mid-September 2026; the FNR news item 'Launch of the first AFdoc call' (16 September 2026) confirms the call is open with a deadline of Wednesday, 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET.

official.application_route: Apply online in English through the FNR Grant Management System (https://grants.fnr.lu/login), with the host institution as the funding recipient and future employer; one proposal per call.
official.citizenship_residency: Applicants must demonstrate a link to Luxembourg (see guidelines for the full definition); the instrument page publishes no nationality restriction.
official.international_eligibility: No nationality restriction is published; eligibility is based on a demonstrated link to Luxembourg, and the PhD may be undertaken at a public PhD-awarding institution abroad.
official.subject_or_agency_requirement: Bottom-up approach: proposals from all fields of research and technological development are eligible; projects do not need to align with Luxembourg's National Research Priorities, provided they fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner.
official.research_requirement: A PhD project proposal prepared and submitted in English via the FNR Grant Management System; the project must fall within the expertise of the supervisors, the Host Institution and, where applicable, the company partner.
official.duration: Funding may cover up to four years of doctoral training.
official.description: AFdoc - Aides a la formation doctorale is a PhD funding scheme, introduced following the entry into force of the new FNR law on 1 August 2026, designed to support talented doctoral candidates with a clear link to Luxembourg who undertake PhD projects in established research environments abroad or through collaborations involving Luxembourg-based companies active in R&D. Funding is granted to eligible Host Institutions, which employ the selected doctoral candidates as beneficiaries through an employment contract.
official.english_requirement: Applications must be submitted in English via the FNR Grant Management System; no IELTS/TOEFL score requirement is published on the instrument page.

applicant_utility.summary: AFdoc is Luxembourg's replacement route for individual PhD funding: you apply with your own doctoral project, but you must already be able to evidence a genuine Luxembourg link, and your host - a public PhD-awarding institution anywhere in the world, or a Luxembourg R&D company accredited by the Minister responsible for the Economy paired with a public PhD-awarding partner - becomes your employer under an employment contract funded up to a maximum of EUR 54,574 per year for up to four years. Because the money follows the employer's salary lines, build the project and budget around the host's payroll and PhD enrolment, and treat tuition, research costs, travel and relocation as separate fundraising problems since they are explicitly ineligible. The live window is the current call closing 25 November 2026 at 14:00 CET, with the next published deadline on 28 April 2027.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Master's graduates who can document a concrete connection to Luxembourg and want a salaried, employment-based PhD at a public university abroad or inside an accredited Luxembourg R&D company.
application_readiness_checklist: Secure the host first: confirm in writing that the public PhD-awarding institution abroad (or the accredited Luxembourg R&D company plus its public PhD-awarding partner) will employ you and enrol you in a PhD programme by the project start date
Assemble documentary proof of your Luxembourg link against the AFdoc guidelines definition well before the call closes - an asserted link with no evidence is the classic failure
Draft the project on the FNR template with a budget built purely on salary lines capped at EUR 54,574 per year including employer charges, social security and pension contributions
Register and test your account in the FNR Grant Management System early so login problems do not consume the deadline
Submit well ahead of 14:00 CET on 25 November 2026 - the portal closes hard and you get only one proposal per call
common_rejection_risks: A Luxembourg link that is claimed but not evidenced the way the guidelines define it

Host institution that is not a public PhD-awarding institution, or a company host that is not accredited by the Minister responsible for the Economy, or a company project lacking the required public-sector PhD-awarding partner
PhD enrolment not secured by the project start date at the time funding is awarded
Budget lines for tuition fees, research costs, travel or installation, all of which are ineligible
Failed or late submission in the Grant Management System - one proposal per call leaves no second attempt
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Tuition fees and related research costs are explicitly not eligible, and no travel or installation allowance is published; enrolment fees, research/consumable costs, relocation and conference travel must be covered by the host institution, the candidate or other funding.
document_audit: The detailed checklist is not on the website: download the application guidelines, project description template and host commitment letter from the AFdoc call-documents folder on the FNR SharePoint early and follow their formatting rules exactly
The commitment letter from the host must describe the same project, supervision environment and employment conditions the reviewers assess - any mismatch reads as an unresolved placement
If your prospective host is a university abroad, check whether it imposes its own internal doctoral-contract deadline earlier than the FNR cut-off
Keep proof of the Luxembourg link (residence, prior study, employment or family-based) in a form a reviewer who has never heard of your situation can read
alerts: This is the very first call of a brand-new scheme created by the new FNR law of 1 August 2026: there is no past results list, so evaluation will hinge strictly on the published criteria
Decision timelines are long: July for the April-deadline call, March of the following year for the November-deadline call, and funded projects must start by 1 February or 1 October respectively

From 2027 the schedule becomes twice-yearly (mid-February launch with end-of-April deadline, mid-September launch with end-of-November deadline), so a miss on 25 November 2026 is not fatal - be ready for April 2027
AFR and Industrial Fellowships are discontinued and point applicants to AFdoc, so do not apply under the old instruments
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: The candidate submits a single English proposal through the FNR Grant Management System by the call deadline; on success the FNR grants funding to the Host Institution, which employs the doctoral candidate under an employment contract of up to four years.
